subject: Flexi prepay ladder & invoice sweep
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@gridscale.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Flexi prepay ladder & invoice sweep

Hi Elena —

Following our demo last week, attached is a proposal that aligns to the usage profile you shared. High level: a 3-year commitment with a flexible prepay ladder so you get term-level discounts while keeping runway for budget cycles. Suggested structure:

- Year 1: 40% prepay at contract signing (applied as credit)
- Year 2: 30% prepay (30 days before the renewal anniversary)
- Year 3: 30% prepay (30 days before the renewal anniversary)

Discounting: 18% on list for the 3-year commitment, with a 2% accelerator for usage >1.2x forecast. Remaining monthly consumption after prepay would be invoiced Net60 by default.

If Net60 is a blocker we can discuss Net90 but we typically require either higher upfront or an alternative risk mitigant (bank guarantee or escrow sweep).

I attached: redwood_proposal_flexi_prepay.pdf for review. Can you confirm who in procurement will own the PO process and whether Gridscale needs a sample bank-guarantee template?

Next steps: if this looks directionally good, Ben and I can prepare a redline-ready SOW and loop in Redwood Finance for an approval path.

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@gridscale.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@gridscale.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Flexi prepay ladder & invoice sweep

David —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear bands. A couple of initial asks from procurement: our standard treasury practice pushes net terms to Net90 for multi-year contracts because our fiscal quarterly planning requires additional approvals.

Net90 is doable on our side, but procurement needs either: (a) a staged invoicing cadence (milestone invoices tied to calendar quarters), (b) an irrevocable bank guarantee covering a portion of committed value, or (c) an escrow with quarterly release based on usage. Can you provide sample language for the bank guarantee or confirm Redwood can accept an escrow arrangement?

I've attached our procurement requirements (gridscale_procurement_requirements.pdf). Procurement is looped in on this thread — they'll own the PO once commercial terms are agreed.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Partnerships
Gridscale Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@gridscale.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Flexi prepay ladder & invoice sweep

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. We can be flexible here. A couple of approaches that have worked for similar customers:

1) Alternate prepay split: 30% / 30% / 40% (moves less cash up front), plus a 10% monthly retainer billed to a short-term invoice to cover ramp months.
2) Milestone invoicing: split the annual committed ARR into quarterly milestone invoices — if you accept Net90 on those, we can align internal forecasting.
3) Bank guarantee: accept an irrevocable bank guarantee that covers 75-80% of committed ARR; that would allow Redwood Finance to approve Net90 on the remaining balance.

I've attached a redline_proposal.pdf with the alternate split and an example clause for escrow. If any of these look good, David and I can get an updated SOW ready.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Flexi prepay ladder & invoice sweep (Finance view)

Hi Elena / team —

Finance reviewed the options. Net90 for multi-year bookings is an exception to our standard terms but we can consider it under these conditions:

- Option A: Minimum 60% prepay at signing across the committed term (reduces working capital exposure).
- Option B: Irrevocable bank guarantee from a Tier 1 bank covering at least 80% of the committed ARR. The guarantee must be unconditional and assignable.
- Option C: Escrow arrangement with quarterly sweeps tied to validated usage metrics; Redwood retains right of release upon agreed thresholds.

If we go with Option B or C, Redwood is comfortable approving Net90 on the residual invoices. We'll need:
- Sample bank-guarantee wording from Gridscale treasury (we can also share our standard wording).
- PO from procurement and an executed SOW.

I've attached a payment_term_matrix.xlsx that maps the commercial levers to internal approval tiers and the expected timeline for finance signoff.

If you confirm which option you prefer, I'll spin up the approval packet and estimate signoff time (typically 5-7 business days for bank guarantee/escrow).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Can you share Redwood's sample bank-guarantee language and an updated SOW (with the 30/30/40 split and milestone invoicing options) so our legal can do a quick review? Also please send DocuSign when the SOW is ready.

I'll expedite the bank side — expect a draft from NovaBank within 3 business days.
